newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Lyonnaise/Suez near merger deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: French Lyonnaise/Suez near merger deal - paper.

text.p: French utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux and conglomerate Cie de Suez are close to wrapping up the terms of a merger, notably the share parity at which they would join forces and "sweeteners" for shareholders, Le Monde newspaper said on Friday.

Both groups declined to comment on the report which quoted sources close to the case as saying the talks had already got to the stage where they "no longer concerned more than the second decimal point" of the share parity to be proposed.

Le Monde said the basis last being worked on set a parity of 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise shares and took account of a payment by Suez of nearly 3.8 billion francs in the form of a normal dividend payout and a special "premium" payment.

"According to our information, the financial company (Suez), which will cancel the shares it owns in itself, is preparing to pay a normal dividend of 8.20 francs per share, in other words totalling 1.27 billion francs," it said. "A 'premium' of 2.5 billion francs would be added to this," it said.

Le Monde also said the question of the board structure for the merged group appeared to be nearing a solution where there would be a single board headed by Lyonnaise boss Jerome Monod until mid-1998, with Suez boss Gerard Mestrallet as vice chairman and managing director and ready to take over the reins.
The two companies have already confirmed they are in merger talks and that their boards will meet to discuss details of the plans on April 11.
